record.file_problem: Only repository metadata, README, and file list are provided; the paper and code contents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a defense-training method that builds on probabilistic ablation of a refusal direction and reports its own defense performance, rather than testing whether the claim's proposed effects hold.
record.gate_note: The README says the method probabilistically ablates the refusal direction during fine-tuning and reports approximately 95% lower attack success rates with downstream performance preserved. These are headline claims about the new method, not results testing the claim versions; no rows are included. The README points to other repositories for refusal-direction extraction and output evaluation.
record.test_reason: V3 includes the clause that training against the direction's ablation adds robustness. DeepRefusal does exactly this: it fine-tunes with probabilistic refusal-direction ablation. It then reports attack-success rates across four model families and six attacks, so its headline result bears on that clause by a different method. The only source here is the README, which gives aggregate claims only.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors also claim the method resists refusal-direction and prefilling attacks, generalizes to unseen jailbreaks, and (per the README news) resists heretic abliteration without performance collapse.
record.recipe_differences: A defense-training approach that probabilistically ablates the direction during fine-tuning, rather than testing the original direct ablation and addition recipe. The README describes a method repository built on Refusal Direction and CircuitBreaker, not a replication.
record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
record.problems: The README provides only headline aggregate performance claims, with no detailed results, baselines, uncertainty, or condition-specific breakdowns. The code and referenced paper were not provided for inspection.
record.rows_left_out: The README's approximately 95% attack-success reduction and performance-preservation claims are excluded because they describe the new defense method's own performance, not a result testing the specified claim versions. No result files appear in the listed repository files.

untested.parts: No ablation/addition test of the direction or capability check of ablation itself is reported in the README.
Whether attacks work by suppressing the direction is not tested; only the training-against-ablation robustness clause is addressed.
No separation of harm judgment and refusal.
No test of how training determines a removable direction. DeepRefusal training plausibly bears on this, but no direction-level analysis is in the README.

missing.what: Per-model, per-attack ASR for DeepRefusal vs. baseline models, including the refusal-direction ablation attack and prefilling, plus capability benchmark scores
missing.locator: Paper arXiv:2509.15202 results tables (not provided); README headline '~95%' claim

missing.what: Heretic (abliteration) attack against the DeepRefusal Llama-3-8B model: refusal rate and capability after the attack

record.verdict_notes: The record treated this as T4 uses_without_test. However, V3 explicitly names 'training against its ablation adds robustness', which is DeepRefusal's headline result, so it is reclassified as a test of that clause. The evidence is README-level only, and the paper should be read to create rows. Both labels are text-based with no row support.

versions.untested_parts: No direct ablation/addition test or measurement of capability preservation is reported.
No weight-edit removal in released models is reported.

The README describes training with probabilistic ablation and overall defense performance, but does not report results testing whether attacks work by suppressing the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
No comparison of one direction with an affine, cone, or multi-direction account is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No transfer results across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models are reported.
No comparison testing how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists is reported.

relationships.condition: Four open-source model families fine-tuned with DeepRefusal (probabilistic refusal-direction ablation across layers and tokens), six attacks including prefilling and refusal-direction attacks
relationships.reason: No rows exist, so this verdict rests on README text: training against ablation cuts attack success 'by approximately 95%' with minimal capability loss. The aggregate figure has no per-condition breakdown.
relationships.display_finding: Training under refusal-direction ablation reportedly reduced aggregate attack success by approximately 95% across four model families and six attacks, with minimal capability loss.

relationships.condition: Llama-3-8B-Instruct after DeepRefusal training, attacked with the heretic abliteration tool
relationships.reason: No rows exist, so this rests on README text only. The authors report that heretic cannot remove safety guardrails without severe performance collapse. This is an informal news-item claim with no numbers.
relationships.display_finding: The authors reported that Heretic could not remove safety guardrails from DeepRefusal-trained Llama-3-8B-Instruct without severe performance collapse.
